correctness.rationale: For all distinct primes \(q,p\) with \(p\ge5\) and integers \(t,r\ge1\), the Jacobsthal lemma gives \(B_j-B_{j-1}\equiv0\pmod{p^{3j}}\); the limit therefore agrees with \(B_r\) modulo \(p^r\). LTE gives \(q^{q^tp^r}\equiv\omega_p(q)^{q^t}\pmod{p^r}\). Legendre gives the exact valuation \(\nu_q(\binom{qn}{n})=s_q((q-1)p^r)/(q-1)\); the other summand is zero modulo \(q^t\). CRT is necessary and sufficient. The endpoint may be zero or infinite, and the limit need not be a unit. For \(q=31,p=5,t=1\), the first two binomials both equal \(251\) modulo \(625\), the Teichmüller root is \(1\), and the endpoint is exactly \(3\). The verifier independently checked 82 direct grid cases and nine boundary cases.

value.rationale: The complete \(q^tp^r\) family is the natural two-prime-support extension of the motivating \(r=1\) theorem and known \(t=0\) towers. At \(t=1\), it gives an exact initial segment and a sharp non-Wieferich cube \(n=31\cdot5^3\). At larger \(t\), it gives a separate digit obstruction: \(q=19,p=7,t=2\) has a nonempty p-adic two-layer segment completely deleted by the digit test. The result distinguishes genuine structural phenomena rather than an arbitrary slice, while claiming no closed formula for all endpoints.
